analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only CI scripts: scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. No provider runtime, coordinator, attestation, encryption, or cache code is modified, so the TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 and T-041 provider paths are unaffected.

What the test changes assert about the workflows:
- Build jobs (build-cluster, build-provider) are now requested and run only when the component's tests run. The BUILT push-refresh-caches path is removed, so a push of an already-tested tree skips the builds too.
- The GPU shards use a new cluster_gpu component.
- The gate now checks a tree-name step and an 'Upload the tree record' step.

Security-relevant properties I checked and found still asserted or unchanged:
- The router job keeps permissions {} and has no secrets, checkout, or id-token.
- Unrouted release and credentialed workflows keep literal runners.
- The watchdog is scoped to this repository with actions/checks write only.
- The unlabel job is the only one with issues/pull-requests write.
- Plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown.
- Sized lanes accept only exactly matching labels.

The diff removes the push cache-refresh build, so it narrows what CI does. Removing that job means fewer cache-save paths, which is not a regression. I could not see the actual workflow files (provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml) or ci-tested-tree.py, so the real workflow changes, including the new tree-name record and the cluster_gpu output, are unverified. The tests may drift from the workflows if those are not changed consistently, and that is the main open integration question. It affects CI integrity only, not a threat-model asset.
